html:
Mohandas Gandhi lived in South Africa from 1893 to 1914, and there he worked out the method of nonviolent mass protest he later used against British rule in India.

He went to Natal at 23 as a lawyer for an Indian trading firm. Soon after arriving he was thrown off a first class train carriage at Pietermaritzburg because he was not white, a moment he later called decisive. He stayed to fight laws against the Indian community, both traders and the workers brought over as indentured labourers, and founded the Natal Indian Congress in 1894.

In 1906 he led Indians in the Transvaal to refuse a law forcing them to register and carry passes. He called the method satyagraha, holding firm to truth: break unjust laws openly and accept jail. He set up communes, the Phoenix Settlement and Tolstoy Farm, named for Leo Tolstoy, with whom he wrote letters. A deal with Jan Smuts in 1914 eased some laws, and Gandhi sailed home, already known as Mahatma.
sum: Mohandas Gandhi lived in South Africa from 1893 to 1914, and there he worked out the method of nonviolent mass protest he later used against British rule in India.
